status: posthoc analysis after Study 4 confirmation results were inspected; NOT a new independent confirmation or preregistration
question: Who changes, why does a same-budget recency baseline remain competitive, and where does candidate pruning lose targets as K grows?
policy: Use frozen Study 4 selection without changes; no fitting, M selection, window search, new user data or changes to old experiment artifacts
fixed_targets: All 8000 users remain; full-history next-basket repeat targets remain the denominator. Recall averages exclude 528 empty targets, with their count reported
seed_aggregation: Average each user's metrics across the three fitted models, not a score ensemble or independent sample expansion
user_diagnostics: Positive, zero and negative paired recall changes; additive population gain/loss contributions; same-budget candidate and top-K overlap, both ordered and unordered lists
subgroup_caution: Historical bins only. Positive/negative outcome-defined groups describe who changed after the fact, not deployable user-selection rules. Marginal intervals are exploratory; no search for a winning subgroup
depth_intervals: Marginal 95% and Bonferroni simultaneous 95% over 12 K/comparator contrasts; exploratory posthoc even after adjustment
depth_ledger: With scores fixed, dual minus full hits equals newly promoted retained true targets minus excluded full-top-K true targets; normalize each user by unchanged R_full
rank_caution: Rank is produced by the existing model. Low predicted rank or observed recall does not imply a product is unimportant or impossible to predict by another model
interpretation: Offline algorithmic decomposition; no human behavioral causality, new-method superiority, measured runtime speedup, storage savings, or confirmed subgroup treatment policy
stop_rule: Finish the stated diagnostics, independent output consistency audit, figures, Chinese narrative and demo update; accept similarities and losses without further model iteration
